cues.text: Datagram packet switching allows independent forwarding decisions, so packets may take different paths.
Virtual circuits establish a logical path.
A permanent virtual circuit is provisioned in advance; a switched virtual circuit is established on demand.
ATM and Frame Relay are historical examples.
MPLS uses label-switched paths, not necessarily a dedicated physical circuit.
Circuit switching has setup, transfer and teardown stages.
Shared packet links are statistically multiplexed.
Here's the longest-prefix example.
Ten dot zero dot zero dot zero slash eight goes through A.
Ten dot one dot zero dot zero slash sixteen goes through B.
Ten dot one dot two dot zero slash twenty-four goes through C.
Ten dot one dot two dot five matches all three, but C wins because slash twenty-four is most specific, regardless of the less specific routes' metrics.
Ten dot one dot nine dot five goes through B.
Now for OSPF: A to B costs ten and B to D costs five, for a total of fifteen.
A to C costs four and C to D costs twenty, totalling twenty-four.
Shortest path first chooses A, B, D.
Both paths have two hops, so hop count cannot distinguish them.
Actual OSPF cost is configured or derived by the implementation.

For the IPv6 documentation example, two thousand and one colon D B eight colon one two three four double colon slash forty-eight can be divided into slash sixty-four LANs using the fourth group ten for staff and twenty for students.
Check the exact prefixes in the visual notes.
Verify router advertisements, neighbour discovery, gateway reachability and IPv6 firewall rules.
IPv4 rules alone aren't sufficient on a dual-stack network.
